channel.title: Cityside Journalism Initiative - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Cityside Journalism Initiative (berkeleyside.org)

item.title: Mt. Agni goes dark, plus the last East Bay outpost of a classic Italian deli has closed
item.description: A running list of restaurants that have recently closed in Berkeley, Oakland, Richmond, and beyond.

item.title: Update: Possible mumps exposure at 2 Berkeley schools, but city says risk of community transmission is ‘very low’
item.description: There were under 350 reported mumps cases in the U.S. last year, the CDC says. The alert comes amid rising misinformation about the vaccine against the contagious disease.

item.title: The Wire: Tabby cat adopted from Berkeley Humane is a top animal actor of the year
item.description: Also: A missing UC Berkeley student was found in Lake Anza and where the Amoeba Music apartment project stands.

item.title: Caught curling fever from the Olympics? Here’s where you can try it in the East Bay
item.description: Berkeleyside news editor Nico Savidge, who once joined a curling club while working at a Wisconsin newspaper, again ventured onto the ice at California's only dedicated curling facility, located in Oakland.

item.title: UC Berkeley cuts ties with nonprofit focused on diversity amid Trump administration pressure
item.description: It is one of 31 colleges that the Education Department says have ended relationships with The PhD Project, a nonprofit that for decades has helped Black, Latino and Native American students get business doctorates.

item.title: What isn’t Berkeley flash fiction master Grant Faulkner doing next?
item.description: He has a new memoir-writing website, a reality TV show and a new book merging short fiction with fine art photography. Other new Berkeley books: Michael Pollan on consciousness — and a deeply researched novel about two famed women pirates of history.

item.title: The rise and fall of the Bay Area’s streetcar transit system
item.description: All nine counties of the Bay Area had robust streetcar systems at the start of the 20th century. In the East Bay, rumors swirl about how and why the Key System failed.

item.title: Developers have found way to bypass Berkeley’s labor standards for housing construction
item.description: Construction unions argue local worker protections are being illegally dismantled. Developers say they’re following state law aimed at lowering the cost of building housing. The City Council is expected to act Monday night.

item.title: Kaiser strike to end after 4 weeks without a deal
item.description: The large, open-ended strike had led to frustrations by some patients over delayed care as well as difficulties for workers who went weeks without a paycheck.

item.title: Berkeley teachers union, school district reach tentative agreement
item.description: The deal, struck after a nearly three-month impasse, came as teachers in next-door Oakland voted to authorize a strike.
